kind.text: PROBE, NOT A DELIVERABLE. This one-page document exists to prove that the run records in this directory are citable by a Doc-IR `claim` -- that the bridge described in `docs/render-2026-08/18-runrec-diary.md` under "Claims on fact cards" is a wiring job and not a research problem. It is hand-written because the producer that will emit these blocks (`facts_to_docir.py`) is owned by another lane; nothing here is generated, and nothing here should be treated as the shape a fact card will finally have. Every number and status on this page comes from a record, not from this file.

note.text: The declared status is `proved`, which is the fact ledger's `epistemic_status` for this entry. Assembly may only lower it, and it does: the first record caps the claim at `checked` because that row's checker matches the theorem's NAME and not its type. The visible gap between the ledger's badge and the rendered badge is the point of the exercise.

statement.text: Addition on the naturals is commutative -- `Nat.add_comm`, admitted by the Lean-style kernel with an empty axiom footprint. Both of the fact ledger's evidence rows for this entry were re-run from the repository root and both exited 0.

kind.label: F:rado-r4-a5-b3, witness and deciding instance replayed

note.text: The witness replay and the CNF regeneration are genuinely different checks over different bytes, so they are cited under different roles. Neither of them re-checks the DRAT refutation that carries the upper bound: the fact's own `axiom_footprint` says `rado.certificate-not-re-checked-per-commit`, and no run record here changes that.

statement.text: The stored colouring for R_4(5(x-y)=3z) > 624 re-verifies from its file, and the deciding CNF at n = 625 comes back byte-identical out of the encoder that produced it.

kind.label: Control: the name-only kernel row notices a restated theorem

note.text: This claim is DELIBERATELY FALSE and is here to be rendered red. The control record exited 0 with `outcome: refuted` -- the mutation was not caught -- and assembly's `refuted` outcome is absorbing, so this claim can only render `refuted` no matter what status this file declares. It is also the only role under which that record may be cited at all.

statement.text: `F:nat-add-comm`'s `kernel-add-comm` row would fail if the kernel admitted a theorem of that name with a different type.
